scope.summary: All six change groups only set pointers to NULL after they are freed. None of them changes an API, a signature, an accepted input or a return contract that the harness relies on. g0001 to g0005 are reached through the harness's parse, print and delete calls and do not change behavior the harness can observe. g0006 (cJSON_free) is never called by the harness. The build foundation cannot be checked because the delegated fuzzing/ossfuzz.sh was not supplied. Lifecycle is also unresolved: the harness frees printed output with free(), and the default global_hooks allocator was not supplied.

assessments.reason: cJSON_Delete now sets item->valuestring and item->string to NULL before the item itself is freed. Nothing reads these fields afterwards, so the harness's delete call behaves the same and the change is still exercised.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Harness calls cJSON_Delete on the parsed tree

assessments.reason: On the parse_string failure path, the local output pointer is now set to NULL after deallocation. Invalid string input reaches this path through cJSON_ParseWithOpts, and the parse still returns false.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Harness parses fuzzer bytes and handles a NULL result

assessments.reason: print() now sets buffer->buffer to NULL after the buffer is moved or freed. The function still returns the same printed pointer. The harness reaches print() through cJSON_Print and cJSON_PrintUnformatted.
On print()'s failure path, buffer->buffer and printed are now set to NULL after being freed. The function still returns NULL, and the harness already handles a NULL result.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Harness calls print and guards against a NULL result

assessments.reason: When print_value fails, cJSON_PrintBuffered now sets the local p.buffer to NULL after freeing it, and still returns NULL. The harness reaches this path through its buffered branch.
cJSON_free only clears its own by-value parameter, so callers cannot observe the change. The complete harness never calls cJSON_free; it uses free() instead.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Harness frees memory with free() and cJSON_Delete, not cJSON_free

build.reason: build.sh hands the whole build to $SRC/cjson/fuzzing/ossfuzz.sh, which was not supplied. The supplied CMake files only define fuzz_main and afl-main, so the actual OSS-Fuzz recipe for this target cannot be checked.

evidence.dependency_reason: Only a non-OSS-Fuzz fuzz_main executable is defined in CMake

input.reason: The harness requires the input to end with a NUL byte and to start with a 4-byte flag prefix before parsing from data+4. strlen in ParseWithOpts is therefore bounded, and every parse option is controlled by the input.

lifecycle.reason: The harness releases cJSON-allocated print output with libc free(). That is only valid if the default global_hooks use malloc/free, and neither the global_hooks definition nor the default allocator was supplied.

evidence.dependency_reason: free() is used on cJSON output
Output is allocated through the hooks

control_flow.reason: Each flag selects one parse, print or minify branch, and every branch is reachable. A parse failure returns before printing. The tree is deleted once on the success path.

evidence.dependency_reason: Parse failure frees internally and returns NULL

missing_information: Contents of fuzzing/ossfuzz.sh, which holds the actual build recipe for cjson_read_fuzzer
Definition of global_hooks and its default allocate/deallocate functions, needed to confirm that freeing print output with free() is valid

assumptions: Each change group consists only of the NULL assignments shown in its added text; the removed text is empty in every group
